title: There Is a Land Mine Eye Hath Seen
description: There Is a Land Mine Eye Hath Seen in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 564 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Better Land”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: There is a land mine eye hath seen, In vi-sions of en-rap-tured thought So bright that all which spreads be-tween Is with its ra-diant glo-ry fraught;

lines: There is a land mine eye hath seen,
So bright that all which spreads between
Is with its radiant glory fraught; —
A land upon whose blissful shore
There rests no shadow, falls no stain;
There those who meet shall part no more,
And those long parted meet again.
Its skies are not like earthly skies,
With varying hues of shade and light;
It hath no need of suns to rise,
To dissipate the gloom of night.
The wanderer there a home may find,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
